topStories.headline: Matt Dorsey Wins Re-Election to Represent SoMa and Mission Bay on the Board of Supervisors
topStories.dek: The District 6 incumbent defeated challenger Alex Behrend in Tuesday's election, securing a second full term representing South of Market, Mission Bay, and surrounding neighborhoods.
topStories.body:
Incumbent Supervisor Matt Dorsey won re-election to the District 6 seat on the San Francisco Board of Supervisors in Tuesday's November 3 consolidated general election, defeating challenger Alex Behrend. Preliminary results from the SF Department of Elections showed Dorsey taking roughly 81 percent of first-choice votes, with the count still being updated as of Thursday afternoon.

District 6 covers South of Market, Rincon Hill, South Beach, Mission Bay, Mid-Market, the Hub, and Showplace Square — a district of about 76,000 residents that has become a focal point in debates over housing, homelessness services, and the future of commercial real estate, with office vacancy rates in parts of SoMa among the highest in the city.

Dorsey was first appointed to the seat in 2022 and won his initial full term that November. His re-election comes on a night that Mission Local described as broadly favorable to Mayor Daniel Lurie's centrist coalition: Lurie's suite of three charter amendments won handily, and Scott Wiener took a commanding lead over Connie Chan in the congressional race to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Final certified results will be posted by the Department of Elections in the weeks ahead.

topStories.headline: Planning Commission Hears Proposal for SoMa's First Gay Bathhouse in Four Decades
topStories.dek: Sanctum Baths, proposed for 12th Street in SoMa, went before the SF Planning Commission Thursday after city planners recommended approval — clearing what may be the last major regulatory hurdle before construction.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Planning Commission heard the application for Sanctum Baths on Thursday, November 6, following a recommendation for approval from SF Planning Department staff. The venue, proposed for a site on 12th Street in SoMa, would be the first new gay bathhouse to open in the neighborhood since the AIDS crisis prompted the forced closure of such establishments in the 1980s.

The project is led by Kevin Born, CEO of Ashbury General Contracting & Engineering, who has described his vision as upscale and explicitly queer-centered. Born initially considered the name Maze SF before settling on Sanctum Baths after working with a marketing consultant. He told the Bay Area Reporter that permitting delays had pushed back his timeline, and he now expects the venue to open by late fall 2027, with an estimated buildout cost of $5 million.

Sanctum Baths would be the first project to result from a 2022 zoning change in which the Board of Supervisors voted 11-0 to allow gay bathhouses and adult sex venues to operate in SoMa, the Castro, and the Tenderloin. Thursday's Planning Commission hearing represented the last significant regulatory hurdle before construction permits can be sought. SFist first reported the pending hearing on November 4.

topStories.headline: SF's Data Center Moratorium Enters Its Review Window — Dogpatch Waterfront Project Remains Frozen
topStories.dek: With Mayor Lurie's signature on the 45-day freeze now three weeks old, the Planning Department's mandatory progress hearing is due this month, keeping a proposed 49.5-megawatt Dogpatch data center in limbo.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's citywide moratorium on new data center approvals, signed by Mayor Daniel Lurie on October 16, is now well into its 45-day clock — and the Planning Department is required to hold a progress hearing before the month ends. The hearing will be the first public accounting of the department's study into data centers' effects on energy consumption, water use, air quality, land use, and surrounding communities.

Two projects are directly frozen by the moratorium: an expansion of NOVVA's existing facility at 400 Paul Avenue in Bayview, and a 49.5-megawatt, roughly 160,000-square-foot data center proposed for 1215 Michigan Street on the Dogpatch waterfront. Permits for the Dogpatch project had been filed by a private equity firm, Nestory Park Capital, which had been in discussions with two of Mayor Lurie's policy chiefs as recently as August. No construction had begun at the site.

The Board of Supervisors passed the moratorium unanimously on October 13, after it was introduced by District 10 Supervisor Shamann Walton, whose district includes Dogpatch and Bayview-Hunters Point. If the planning study finds significant environmental impact, the moratorium can be extended to roughly 22 months — and sources close to Walton's office say the supervisor hopes it leads to permanent controls. San Francisco currently has no land-use definition for data centers and no rules specifically targeting their water or power demands. The November progress hearing is the next concrete milestone to watch.

events.title: 27th Annual Potrero Hill & Dogpatch History Night
events.location: Pier 70 Time Machine, Building 12, 420 22nd Street, Dogpatch
events.description: The Pier 70 Time Machine hosts the 27th edition of this free annual gathering, featuring a photography exhibition by Henrik Kam, a 100th-anniversary celebration of the Potrero Boosters Neighborhood Association, and a conversation about the history of Jackson Playground Park. Live music, pizza, and beverages begin at 5:30 p.m.; the historical program runs 7–9 p.m.

events.title: Make a Kite with Jacob Hashimoto at SFMOMA
events.description: Artist Jacob Hashimoto leads a hands-on kite-making workshop inside his new installation Giant Arc, an immersive canopy of nearly 70,000 kites suspended across the Roberts Family Gallery. Included with museum admission.

events.title: Chuck Sperry: Archetypes — Harman Projects
events.description: Dogpatch's Minnesota Street Project galleries host the opening week of a new solo exhibition by concert poster artist Chuck Sperry. Free admission; gallery hours run Tuesday through Saturday.

events.title: SOMArts Día de Los Muertos: 'In Their Name' — Closing Soon
events.location: SOMArts Cultural Center, 934 Brannan Street, SoMa
events.description: SOMArts' 27th annual Día de Los Muertos exhibition, honoring mothers and acts of care, runs through November 20. The show is part of SOMArts' active programming season as the organization works to close a budget gap — donations are welcome at somarts.org.

events.title: Mission Bay Commute Survey 2026
events.description: The Mission Bay Transportation Management Association's annual three-minute commuter survey is open through November 25 at 11:59 p.m. Results inform future shuttle routes, SFMTA planning priorities, and commuter programs for everyone who travels to and from Mission Bay.

moreNews.headline: Potrero Annex Demolition Underway as HOPE SF Redevelopment Advances
moreNews.body: Demolition of the Potrero Annex public housing complex on Potrero Hill was confirmed underway as of June 2026, according to the Potrero View — a major milestone in a rebuild plan launched nearly 20 years ago. The Potrero Annex and Terrace project is part of HOPE SF, the city's program to replace distressed public housing with mixed-income communities. The cleared site moves the long-delayed project closer to new construction, though the broader Annex-Terrace redevelopment has faced persistent setbacks since it was first proposed in 2005.

moreNews.headline: Mission Bay Shuttle Stop at 7th and YOTEL Rerouted Through November 19
moreNews.body: Mission Bay shuttle riders should note that the stop at 7th Street and YOTEL is temporarily inaccessible through November 19 due to active construction at the intersection. During this period, the Mission Bay TMA shuttle is boarding in front of 1083 Market Street. Riders are advised to check missionbaytma.org for real-time updates.

restaurants.name: Californios
restaurants.description: The world's first three-Michelin-star Mexican restaurant, helmed by chef Val M. Cantú, serving an inventive tasting menu rooted in Mexican and Northern California ingredients.

restaurants.name: Benu
restaurants.description: Chef Corey Lee's three-Michelin-star flagship, ranked among the world's 50 best restaurants, serving an Asian-inspired tasting menu in an intimate SoMa setting.

restaurants.name: Montesacro SOMA
restaurants.description: Beloved SoMa pinseria serving Rome's ancient oval flatbread — pinsa — made from a blend of wheat, rice, and soy flour, with an excellent Italian wine list.

restaurants.name: Plow
restaurants.description: A beloved Potrero Hill corner café open since 2010, drawing loyal queues for its lemon ricotta pancakes, crispy potatoes, and locally sourced egg plates.

restaurants.name: Chez Maman East

restaurants.name: Marcella's Lasagneria

restaurants.name: Wooly Pig
restaurants.description: A popular Dogpatch neighborhood spot known for bold, Asian-influenced sandwiches, plates, and fresh seasonal ingredients in a relaxed setting.

restaurants.name: Long Bridge Pizza
restaurants.description: A Dogpatch favorite known for thoughtfully topped, well-priced pies and a casual, community-minded atmosphere near the waterfront.

restaurants.name: Piccino Restaurant
restaurants.description: A Dogpatch-adjacent Cal-Italian hangout with thin-crust pizzas, milk-braised pork ragù, walk-up bar seating, and a covered parklet ideal for daytime dining.

restaurants.name: Sohn
restaurants.description: A spacious Dogpatch warehouse conversion with Korean-inflected dishes — popcorn chicken, cold noodles, taco bar — and a low-key vibe suited for weekday dates or weekend crowds.

restaurants.name: Ungrafted
restaurants.description: Founded by Master Sommelier Rebecca Fineman, Ungrafted pairs an impressive, approachable wine list with thoughtfully crafted food in a relaxed Dogpatch setting.

restaurants.name: Mission Rock Resort
restaurants.description: A beloved SF Legacy Business at the water's edge near Oracle Park, serving fresh Dungeness crab deviled eggs, clam chowder, and $1 oysters at happy hour.
restaurants.address: 817 Terry Francois Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94158

restaurants.name: ATwater Tavern
restaurants.description: A Mission Bay waterfront tavern popular on Giants game days, offering American pub fare and a broad drink menu steps from Oracle Park.

restaurants.name: Burma Love
restaurants.description: A Mission Bay outpost of the popular Burma Love brand, serving Burmese staples including tea leaf salad, rainbow salad, and coconut noodle dishes near Thrive City.
restaurants.address: 3 Mission Rock St, San Francisco, CA 94158

restaurants.name: Dabao Singapore
restaurants.description: A five-year SoMa institution serving authentic Singaporean classics — five-spice Hainanese chicken rice, Char Kway Teow noodles — in an unfussy, minority-owned setting.

restaurants.name: SF Kebab
restaurants.description: A reliable Mission Bay family restaurant offering Mediterranean kebabs, rice, and salads with indoor and outdoor seating, popular with UCSF campus visitors.

restaurants.name: Dogpatch Saloon
restaurants.description: A beloved Dogpatch dive bar with a loyal dog-friendly following, craft cocktails, and late-night hours — open daily from 2 p.m. through 2 a.m.

restaurants.name: Third Rail
restaurants.description: A Dogpatch cocktail bar known for creative drinks alongside housemade beef and candy jerky, with shot-beer-jerky combos that keep regulars coming back.

restaurants.name: Bar Piccino
restaurants.description: A refined Dogpatch cocktail bar with a full Negroni menu, creative non-alcoholic cocktails, mezcal flights, and Oyster Sundays in an intimate setting.

restaurants.name: Giuliana's Just for You Café

restaurants.description: A cheerful Potrero Hill/Dogpatch café serving New American brunch with fresh-baked bread, locally sourced ingredients, and unforgettable beignets.

hotels.name: The St. Regis San Francisco
hotels.description: A 260-room Forbes Five-Star luxury hotel in the heart of SoMa, directly adjacent to SFMOMA and Yerba Buena Gardens, with the Museum of the African Diaspora housed within the property.

hotels.name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco Downtown SoMa
hotels.description: A 686-room, 36-story SoMa tower comprehensively renovated in 2022, two blocks from Moscone Center, with on-site restaurant La Societe and one of the city's largest hotel fitness studios.

hotels.name: InterContinental San Francisco
hotels.description: A 550-room SoMa hotel with an indoor pool, restaurant, and bar, convenient to Moscone Convention Center and the Yerba Buena arts district.

hotels.name: Hotel Via
hotels.description: A modern 159-room boutique hotel directly across the street from Oracle Park in Mission Bay, featuring a rooftop terrace bar with sweeping views of the Bay.

hotels.name: Canopy by Hilton San Francisco SoMa
hotels.description: A 4-star lifestyle hotel on 4th Street in SoMa, minutes from Yerba Buena Gardens and Moscone Center, known for its welcoming staff and locally inspired design.

hotels.name: SoMa House
hotels.description: A newly renovated independent hotel at 7th and Market offering a heated rooftop pool, valet parking, and the soon-to-open SoMa Social gastropub, steps from Moscone Center.

hotels.name: LUMA Hotel San Francisco
hotels.description: A sleek boutique hotel in Mission Bay's South Beach district, a seven-minute walk from Oracle Park, with a fitness center, restaurant, and bar.

shops.name: SFMOMA Museum Store
shops.description: The West Coast's finest selection of modern and contemporary art books, design objects, jewelry, stationery, and exclusive SFMOMA signature products, open to museum visitors and the public.

shops.name: Christopher's Books
shops.description: A beloved independent bookstore tucked into a corner in Potrero Hill, offering a curated selection of fiction, nonfiction, and local-interest titles with a warm community feel.

shops.name: Cole Hardware – SoMa
shops.description: A locally owned 6,000-square-foot hardware and home store at 9th and Folsom, stocking everything from tools and paint to housewares and garden supplies.

shops.name: San Francisco Flower Market
shops.description: One of the nation's largest cut-flower wholesale markets, open to the public from early morning, with dozens of vendors offering fresh-cut blooms, plants, and floral supplies.

shops.name: Revel Shop
shops.type: Women-owned neighborhood gift and lifestyle shop
shops.description: A charming, locally and women-owned Dogpatch boutique carrying curated gifts, home goods, stationery, and lifestyle items for the neighborhood community.

shops.name: Dogpatch Games
shops.type: Board game shop and event space
shops.description: A neighborhood-loved Potrero Hill game shop and event space stocking tabletop games, card games, and RPGs, with regular game nights and community events.

shops.name: Nicolehollis Collection
shops.type: Luxury design objects gallery and shop
shops.description: Interior designer Nicole Hollis's first brick-and-mortar shop at Minnesota Street Project, selling 200-plus limited-edition artisan pieces — decor, textiles, tabletop, and scents — drawn from 25 years of private-client sourcing.

shops.name: DECANTsf
shops.description: A carefully curated SoMa wine shop on Folsom Street focused on small-production and artisan wines, offering knowledgeable staff and a welcoming neighborhood atmosphere.

shops.name: Mainstay Markets
shops.description: A Dogpatch market committed to healthy eating and local businesses, stocking locally sourced produce, specialty grocery items, and pantry staples.

shops.name: The Box SF
shops.description: A beloved SoMa multi-vendor vintage and consignment space housed in a historic print shop, drawing shoppers with its maze-like layout and eclectic selection.

artEntertainment.name: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art (SFMOMA)
artEntertainment.description: The largest modern art museum in the United States, with seven floors of galleries and 33,000+ works; the new RM x SFMOMA exhibition opens October 3, 2026 and runs through February 2027.

artEntertainment.name: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts (YBCA)
artEntertainment.description: SoMa's 33-year-old cultural anchor presenting contemporary art, performance, and film across two landmark buildings, with current exhibitions including GaHee Park: Behind the Curtain (through January 3, 2027) and Dread Scott: The Body Politic (through January 31, 2027); open Wed–Sun, with free Wednesdays extended to 8 p.m.

artEntertainment.name: Minnesota Street Project
artEntertainment.description: A flagship Dogpatch arts campus housing multiple contemporary galleries, studios, and the newly opened Ruth Asawa Lanier, Inc. gallery — the first permanent public home for Ruth Asawa's wire sculptures, drawings, and community projects.

artEntertainment.name: Museum of the African Diaspora (MoAD)
artEntertainment.description: A SoMa museum housed within the St. Regis Hotel dedicated to the art, history, and culture of the African Diaspora, with rotating exhibitions and community programming.

artEntertainment.name: Children's Creativity Museum
artEntertainment.type: Interactive children's arts and technology museum
artEntertainment.description: A hands-on Yerba Buena museum for children up to age 12, featuring a stop-animation studio, digital media lab, and interactive exhibits at the edge of Yerba Buena Gardens.

artEntertainment.name: 111 Minna Gallery
artEntertainment.type: Contemporary art gallery and events space
artEntertainment.description: A SoMa gallery and event venue showcasing rotating works by local and international contemporary artists in an intimate urban space near Yerba Buena.

artEntertainment.name: SOMArts Cultural Center
artEntertainment.description: A city-funded SoMa arts center supporting diverse Bay Area artists through gallery exhibitions, education, and residency programs, with year-round community programming.

artEntertainment.name: Oracle Park
artEntertainment.type: Major league baseball stadium and live events venue
artEntertainment.description: Home of the San Francisco Giants since 2000, Oracle Park is a premier waterfront stadium in Mission Bay hosting baseball, concerts, and special events, with the 2026 MLB season underway.
artEntertainment.address: 24 Willie Mays Plaza, San Francisco, CA 94107

artEntertainment.name: American Bookbinders Museum
artEntertainment.type: Specialty bookbinding and printing history museum
artEntertainment.description: A unique SoMa museum preserving the history of the bookbinding trade through rare presses, tools, and beautifully bound book displays, with a charming gift shop.

gymsRecreation.name: Dogpatch Boulders
gymsRecreation.description: Northern California's premier bouldering-only facility, with 20,500 square feet of climbing terrain, 300+ boulder problems, world-class routesetting, and yoga and fitness classes for all levels.

gymsRecreation.name: FITNESS SF – SoMa
gymsRecreation.description: A sprawling full-block SoMa fitness center open until midnight on weekdays, offering cardio, free weights, strength conditioning, and group fitness classes.

gymsRecreation.name: Ritual Hot Yoga – SoMa
gymsRecreation.description: A highly rated SoMa hot yoga studio offering hot power fusion, Yin yoga, and heated flow classes in a clean, well-equipped, community-focused environment.

gymsRecreation.name: CorePower Yoga – Mission Bay

gymsRecreation.name: 3rd Street Boxing Gym
gymsRecreation.description: A Dogpatch boxing institution founded by Gold Gloves champion Wade, offering boxing training and fitness classes for all levels in an authentic gym environment.

gymsRecreation.name: LuxFit Mission Rock

gymsRecreation.address: 1 Mission Rock St, San Francisco, CA 94158
